description: ignorePaths restates :ignoreModulesAndTests without **/examples/**, so the example Containerfiles and manifests track the same versions the shipped images do. The field is not mergeable, so dropping one entry means listing them all.

packageRules.description: config:recommended pulls in :semanticPrefixFixDepsChoreOthers, which types production dependencies as fix and everything else as chore. Release notes then split identical dependency bumps across Fixed and Changed, so type them all as chore.
Auto-merge non-major updates once they have aged a day. GitHub's own auto-merge holds each PR until the required checks pass, so groups land independently rather than one per run.
A digest bump is the same tag rebuilt, usually for a CVE patch, and carries no release notes to age. Soaking it would also never converge: each rebuild restarts the clock.
One PR per ecosystem, as Dependabot grouped them. Majors stay separate so a breaking change is never bundled with an automerged bump.

Same-version updates get their own branch rather than joining an ecosystem group. A digest or pin leaves newValue unchanged, so grouping one alongside a version bump for the same dependency gives the branch two targets and Renovate discards the collision. Split per manager so one dependency Renovate cannot rewrite does not abandon every other digest.
A major is a breaking change: its own PR, ungrouped, reviewed by a human.
No workflow tests .devcontainer, so these land as a PR for a human rather than automerging unchecked.
scripts/set-version.sh owns every g0efilter pin and tests/repo asserts they equal VERSION, so Renovate must not move them.
The Go toolchain is pinned in the workflows as well, so it is bumped deliberately rather than by a PR that would desync the two.
curl and k3s are throwaway test and demo peers, wanted at whatever latest is rather than at a recorded version. Un-ignoring examples/ would otherwise start pinning them.

workarounds:all teaches Renovate that chart-testing-action's version input tracks the helm/chart-testing CLI, so the dep resolves against that repo while the only text to rewrite is the action's uses line. A digest from the CLI repo does not exist in the action repo, so pinning one can never be applied and fails the whole branch.
